text.p: C-TEC Corp, which owns 62 percent of Mercom Inc, on Monday said it was suspending discussions over the possible acquisition of the remaining 38 percent of the cable television operator.
In May, C-TEC said it would acquire the rest of Mercom after a restructuring in which C-TEC would become three separate, publicly traded companies.
In a statement Monday, C-TEC said it was suspending talks with Mercom until completing the restructuring, which is expected before year's end.

"We still think that the combination of the Mercom and C-TEC Michigan cable operations is a good idea that would benefit all shareholders. But we have a duty to the C-TEC shareholders to first ensure the C-TEC restructuring is complete," the C-TEC statement said.
The company said the restructuring is subject regulatory approvals and certain other conditions. There are no assurances that any transaction would take place, it said.
In the same statement, Mercom said it agreed to sell its 1,875-subscriber cable system in Port St. Lucie, Florida, to Adelphia Communications Corp for $3.75 million.

Mercom serves 40,000 subscribers in three clusters of cable television systems in southern Michigan. Mercom operates under management of C-TEC Cable Systems of Michigan Inc, a subsidiary of C-TEC Corp.
C-TEC, headquartered in Princeton, N.J., is a telecommunications company whose operating divisions include RCN Telecom Services, Commonwealth Telephone Co and C-TEC Cable Systems.
